overview: A Pacific Northwest storm moves across the Rockies through Friday and Saturday, with snow falling hardest in northern Utah and western Wyoming first. Snow fades on the weekend, and a weaker system follows early next week.

regions.title: Wasatch
regions.text: A Pacific Northwest storm brings snow to the Wasatch through early Saturday, focused on the northern mountains as it moves east. Snow levels drop Friday night, bringing accumulating snow to northern valley floors. Powder Mountain leads with 10" total, and the National Weather Service says it could see 12 to 20 inches from Friday through Monday. A Winter Storm Warning runs from Thursday to Saturday.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: A system brings heavier snow to the western mountains and passes Thursday night into Friday, with the Tetons under a winter weather advisory. Snow shifts east Friday afternoon, bringing snow to southern and central Wyoming and possible travel trouble on I-80. Cooler, unsettled weather follows through the weekend and early next week. Grand Targhee leads with 10" total.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Moist southwest flow brings banded snow to the high mountains Thursday night into Saturday, with gusty winds up to 45 mph on higher terrain. Snow is most likely in the Elk, Flat Tops and Park ranges, and the eastern Uintas may see more. Telluride and Crested Butte each show about 7" in total. Another chance of snow arrives Monday.

ahead.text: The Weather Prediction Center says a wet pattern will return to the Intermountain West and Rockies after Thanksgiving week's start, with rain and mountain snow expected on Wednesday Nov 25. The Climate Prediction Center expects a weaker trough in the West around Thursday Nov 26.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
